pixel_findings: The exact allotment identity remains legible: straight shared route, individually fenced garden plots, coloured timber sheds, planted crop beds and rear orchard lawns.
Eight mixed beds now combine low rosettes, narrow upright crop leaves and supported vines; walking and detail views show distinct plant heights and silhouettes instead of identical dome canopies.
Planting remains inside beds and plots; crop supports contact soil and do not intrude into central or plot-entry routes.
Sheds, benches, trellises, fence posts, beds and hedge foliage are grounded and coherent in the native clay material tier.
Both end openings remain unobstructed through fence and hedge; plot entrances remain visible and reachable.
Stone path edges, shed pavers, soil beds and gravel marks provide readable ground ownership and pedestrian detail.
Whole-scene views retain complete boundary and safety margin. Phone comparisons preserve source programme at site scale.

Conservatory benchmark comparison supports the composed-plan and pedestrian-finish native clay gate: authored crop programme, readable routes, detailed borders and complete grounded geometry. This is not a claim of photographic equivalence.
p2_followups: Additional botanical species and less regular maturation could enrich future garden versions without changing this usable native programme.
A future phone-front board could pair the reference with walk.png for a closer pedestrian camera match; current walk and plot_walk files were directly reviewed.
limitations: Native clay geometric/material tier; no photoreal texture or botanical simulation approval.
No browser, terrain, fit, resizing, editing, persistence, capture or runtime performance claim.
No human visual activation or publication approval.
scale_up_scope: Visual pilot supports one bounded next park candidate; every new candidate requires its own review.
